questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel overly confident.
It reduces your ability to think clearly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, reduces coordination and balance, and impairs your vision. Your ability to judge distance also suffers, making it harder to respond to what is happening around you.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow at a traffic light, you should:

options.text: Wait until the light turns solid green.
Stop, then turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
Turn in the direction shown by the arrow if the intersection is clear.
Speed up and turn quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction shown by the arrow if the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you have the right-of-way to turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane to make this turn. Always stay alert for other drivers and pedestrians who may be in the intersection illegally.

questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal traffic rules as if no children are present.

questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard, sign, or police officer in a school zone. Drive slowly and carefully in these areas to protect children.

questions.question: You can reduce road rage and aggressive driving by:

options.text: Leaving extra travel time.
Following posted speed limits.
Using your turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip. These actions help reduce tension on the road for all drivers.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare at the road for a long time without looking around.
You take frequent rest stops.
You get too much sleep before driving.
You drive short distances on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for a long time without looking around.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you focus straight ahead without looking side to side or checking your mirrors. This causes you to zone out and miss hazards, especially cars that are slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: Road markings:

options.text: Are not very important.
Are only used in construction zones.
Help guide drivers on the road.
Are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help guide drivers on the road.
questions.explanation: Road markings help drivers stay in their lanes, show where it is safe to pass, and warn drivers about upcoming conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and honk your horn.
A bus stop is near.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children in this area.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less of the road. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.
Not drive if you feel tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, visibility is lower. Take these steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe in the dark.

questions.question: To avoid hitting the car in front of you, you should:

options.text: Watch for hazards ahead.
Watch for brake lights.
Use the four-second rule for following distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent rear-end crashes, watch for brake lights and other hazards ahead. Keep a four-second distance between your car and the car in front under normal driving conditions.

questions.question: To drive safely, what should you do about your physical condition?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Only drive within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe. Stay fit, get check-ups, and understand how medicine affects you.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or leaving a curb. Do not skip this step even when the road seems empty. Make it a habit to always signal.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Entering or leaving a parking space.
Moving into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal for any movement left or right. This includes changing lanes, entering or leaving parking spaces, and pulling into traffic from alleys or parking areas. Signals help other drivers stay safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross.
Come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians pass first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Tiredness while driving is as dangerous as drunk driving. If you feel tired, stop driving right away.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Make turning harder.
Increase the risk of hydroplaning.
Increase how far it takes to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning difficult, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Entering or leaving a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal for any movement left or right. Signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving parking spaces, and pulling into traffic from alleys or parking areas.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of their way.
Stare at the driver as they pass.
Speed up as they are passing.
Block the passing lane.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up or block them, as this makes them angrier and more dangerous.
